Will —

Thanks for the clear priorities. I've sketched an initial test matrix and acceptance criteria we can use in the MAP. Key points below; full test cases are in DS_MAP_TestCases.csv (attached to the MAP).

Test matrix (short summary):
- Workload A (chat): seq_len 75 tokens, dynamic batching up to 8 concurrent requests, target endpoints: 95th percentile latency target = 250ms, TTFT target = <40ms for warmed caches.
- Workload B (rerank batch): seq_len 200 tokens, throughput target = sustained 1.2M tokens/min for nightly window.

GPU variants to evaluate (each with full GPU vs MIG when supported):
- NVIDIA A100 (40GB) — baseline for prior runs
- NVIDIA H100 (80GB) — expected better throughput and perf at scale
- NVIDIA L40S (48GB) — cost-focused, optimized for large batch throughput, slightly higher TTFT in some microbenchmarks

Metrics to capture per-run:
- Wall-clock latency distribution (P50/P95/P99)
- TTFT (time to first token) — cold vs warmed KV-cache scenarios
- Throughput (tokens/s) and effective RPS at target latency SLOs
- GPU utilization, memory headroom, and avg KV cache hits

Acceptance criteria (preliminary):
- Chat: P95 <= 250ms and TTFT <= 40ms for warmed runs on the chosen fleet
- Batch: achieves 1.2M tokens/min within the maintenance window at <= 70% GPU utilization
Sizing note for MIG vs full GPU tests:
- We recommend running MIG carve-outs at 1/2 and 1/4 profiles where available to see latency isolation. MIGs can be cost-effective for low-latency, low-concurrency workloads but may hit higher TTFT under bursty traffic.

I've attached a CSV with test cases and a short appendix PDF with example command-lines we will run.

If this looks good, we will start PoC runs Monday and share the raw results spreadsheet by end of week.

— Sergio

Will/Sergio —

Adding a few technical sizing notes based on similar customers and our internal runs. These are estimates to help procurement frame options; final numbers will come from the PoC.

Assumptions for chat workload (A): average prompt 75 tokens + model 8B-ish dense decoder, typical serving config (kv cache warmed for active sessions).

Estimated single-GPU sustained RPS (approx):
- A100 (40GB, full): ~320 requests/s sustained at P95 ~220ms, TTFT warmed ~38ms
- H100 (80GB, full): ~520 requests/s sustained at P95 ~180ms, TTFT warmed ~28ms
- L40S (48GB, full): ~410 requests/s sustained at P95 ~240ms, TTFT warmed ~45ms

MIG carve-out expectations (per GPU):
- A100 1/2-MIG: ~150 req/s, slightly higher TTFT (+10–15ms)
- H100 1/4-MIG: ~120–160 req/s depending on profile, TTFT +15–25ms under burst

Sizing snapshots (for 20k concurrent active chat sessions with typical interleaving):
- If low-latency P95 target <= 200ms: recommend H100 full GPU fleet; ballpark 40 H100 GPUs (with autoscale headroom)
- If cost-first and willing to accept P95 <= 250ms: hybrid L40S + A100 baseline; ballpark 60 L40S or 45 A100
- MIG-heavy consolidation (best fit for large multi-tenant non-burst workloads): equivalent of 70x 1/4-MIG partitions across A100/H100/L40S depending on VM profile; expect TTFT penalty during spikes.

Cost delta (rough monthly compute-only):
- H100 full fleet > A100 full fleet by ~30–45% depending on region and utilization.
- L40S full fleet ~15–25% cheaper than A100 for throughput workloads, but may require more nodes for low-latency SLOs.

Recommendation: run quick A/B PoC across one H100 and one L40S node with identical traffic replay (chat) and a separate A100 MIG run. We will capture P95/TTFT and project scaling to your target QPS.

I'll prep a short appendix with the exact kernel configs we will use and the commands for reproducing the runs.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Will — Sergio — Karthik — Tessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. This thread is the canonical MAP for the eval; I've attached the completed MAP and a raw results workbook (DS_MAP_PerfResults_Q42026.xlsx) that contains the run-level metrics from our lab. Quick summary / next steps below: 

Summary of PoC (executive):
- Chat (prioritized): H100 delivers best low-latency headroom (P95 ~180ms, TTFT ~28ms warmed); L40S hit throughput targets but had slightly higher TTFT (~45ms) under burst. A100 baseline sits between the two.
- Batch rerank: All three GPUs achieved the nightly throughput target when configured with larger batch windows; L40S offered the best cost/token for purely throughput runs.
- MIG: viable for consolidation but introduces a measurable TTFT penalty during bursts (+15–25ms), so we recommend MIGs only for background or non-interactive workloads.

Recommended path to close (MAP milestones and dates):
- 2026-10-30: Redwood delivers one-page cost-delta and finalized MAP (attachment: hw_comparison_appendix.pdf) — ACTION: Redwood (Rachel)
- 2026-11-03: DataScale infra pilot sign-off (canary deployment runbook) — ACTION: DataScale (Will)
- 2026-11-08: Procurement review packet due — ACTION: DataScale (Procurement)
- 2026-11-10: Executive approval meeting (internal DataScale) — ACTION: DataScale
- 2026-11-17: Target PO date / contract execution — ACTION: Both

Canary rollout (short):
- Phase 0: Small internal traffic replay in Redwood staging with identical routing to production (2 hours)
- Phase 1: 5% production traffic to H100 pool for 24 hours (monitor P95/TTFT and error rate)
- Phase 2: 25% traffic for 48 hours, validate autoscaling and fallback routes to A100 pool
- Phase 3: Full roll pending go/no-go signoff
